I: C2 [ I ] to jump on one foot or to move about in this way
C2 [ I ] If a small animal, bird, or insect hops, it moves by jumping on all or two of its feet at the same time.
I + adv/prep: C1 [ I + adv/prep ] informal to go somewhere quickly or to get into or out of a vehicle quickly
快速去（某地）；快速跳上（或跳下）（車輛）

C: › [ C ] a short jump by a person on one foot, or by a small animal, bird, or insect on all or two of its feet at the same time
單足短距離跳躍；（小動物、鳥或昆蟲的）齊足（或雙足）短距離跳躍
› to be a short distance, especially by plane

NONE: › the dried fruits of a climbing plant, used to give a bitter flavour to beer

example: I tried to hop on my good foot while holding onto Jim.
我抓住吉姆，並用我那隻好腳努力向前跳。
We hopped over to Bruges for the weekend.
我們飛速趕到布魯日去度週末。
I hopped on the bus at the traffic lights.
我在紅綠燈處匆匆跳上公共汽車。
The rabbit/bird hopped across the grass.
兔子／鳥蹦跳著穿過草地。
With his feet tied together he could only move in little hops.
他雙腳被捆在一起，只能小步跳。
Rio to São Paulo is just a short hop by plane.
乘飛機的話，從裡約到聖保羅只是很短的一段路。
a hop plant
啤酒花植株

NONE: › used to tell someone to go away
A2 to want something to happen or to be true, and usually have a good reason to think that it might
B1 something good that you want to happen in the future, or a confident feeling about what will happen in the future

example: I'm hoping for an interview next week.
我盼望著下星期有一次面試。
[ + (that) ] She's hoping (that) she won't be away too long.
她希望她不會離開太久。
I hope (that) she'll win.
我希望她能贏。
We have to hope and pray (that) the operation will go well.
我們只能祈禱手術順利。
[ + to infinitive ] They hope to visit us next year.
他們希望明年能來我們這裡作客。
It's good news, I hope.
我希望是好消息。
"Will you be at the meeting tomorrow?" "I hope not/so".
｢你明天會參加那個會議嗎？｣ ｢恐怕不行／我想是的。｣
What are your hopes and dreams for the future?
你對未來有甚麼希望和夢想？
Is there any hope of getting financial support for the project?
這個案子有沒有希望得到資金上的援助?
[ + that ] Is there any hope that they will be home in time?
他們有沒有希望及時回到家?
Young people are growing up in our cities without any hope of finding a job.
城市裡的年輕人一天天長大，卻根本沒有希望找到工作。
His reply dashed (= destroyed) our hopes.
他的回答使我們的希望破滅。
They have pinned (all) their hopes on (= they are depending for success on) their new player.
他們把（所有）希望都寄託在新隊員身上。
She's very ill, but there's still hope/we live in hope (= we think she might be cured).
她病得非常嚴重，但是仍有希望／我們覺得仍有希望。
The situation is now beyond/past hope (= unlikely to produce the desired result).
現在的情況已經毫無希望了。
We never gave up hope (= stopped hoping) that she would be found alive.
我們從未放棄她能夠生還的希望。
The letter offered us a glimmer/ray of (= a little) hope.
這封信給了我們一線希望。
I didn't phone until four o'clock in the hope that you'd be finished.
我一直到四點才打電話是希望這時你就已經完成了。
I don't hold out much hope of getting (= I don't expect to be able to get) a ticket.
我對得到票不抱多大希望。

NONE: › to hope very strongly that something will happen, although you know it is not likely
抱著萬一的希望，存一線希望

example: They're just hoping against hope that she's still alive.
他們對她還活著仍抱一線希望。

NONE: › clothes, sheets, etc. that a young woman traditionally collects for use after she is married

example: Kate's grandmother gave her a quilt for her hope chest.
凱特的祖母給她的嫁妝添了一條被子。

NONE: › to hope that something will be successful or happen in the way you want, even if it seems unlikely
抱樂觀的態度，盡量往好處想

example: I've repaired it as well as I can - we'll just have to hope for the best.
我已經盡力修理——我們只能盡量往好處想了。

NONE: › said when you continue to hope that something will happen, although it seems unlikely
希望之泉永不枯竭；希望常在
（用於強調）真的希望／衷心希望／向天發誓

example: I hope to God (that) he turns up.
我真希望他能露面。
I swear to God (that) I didn't know about it.
我向天發誓我對此一無所知。

NONE: 抱有希望的，充滿希望的
› a person who is trying to get a part in a film, play for a famous sports team, etc.
希望成名的人（設法參與電影拍攝，戲劇演出，著名足球俱樂部等等）

example: He was hopeful about the outcome of the meeting.
他對會議的結果充滿希望。
They were hopeful of a successful agreement.
他們對成功達成協議充滿希望。
I'm hopeful (that) we can reach a compromise.
我對我們能達成和解充滿希望。
The green shoots were hopeful signs of spring.
綠色的嫩芽是春天充滿希望的象徵。
Over a thousand young hopefuls went to the Theatre Royal today to audition for a part in the new musical.
一千多名希望成名的年輕人今天去皇家劇院，參加那齣新音樂劇其中一個角色的試鏡。

NONE: B1 used, often at the start of a sentence, to express what you would like to happen

example: Hopefully it won't rain.
但願老天不會下雨。
Hopefully we'll be in Norwich by early evening.
但願我們在傍晚時分能到達諾裡奇。
"Do you have a cigarette?" he asked hopefully.
｢你有香煙嗎？｣他滿懷希望地問道。

NONE: B2 completely without skill at a particular activity

example: a hopeless situation
毫無希望的局勢
They searched for survivors but it was hopeless.
他們搜尋生還者，但沒有任何希望。
She was depressed and felt totally hopeless about the future.
她情緒低落，覺得未來毫無希望。
I'm hopeless at sports.
我在體育方面糟透了。
He's a hopeless cook.
他做菜一塌糊塗。

NONE: C2 extremely, or in a way that makes you lose hope

example: They met at university and fell hopelessly in love.
他們在上大學時相遇，並無可救藥地墜入愛河。
We were hopelessly lost.
我們徹底迷路了。

NONE: › a large tube, wide at one end, through which large amounts of small separate things, for example seeds, can be moved from one container to another
› like hops (= dried fruit used to make beer)

example: a hoppy aroma/flavour
啤酒花般的芳香/味道

NONE: › a game played by children, who throw a stone onto a set of joined squares drawn on the ground and jump on one leg and then on two legs into each square to get the stone
